name: External Roles
description: Framework module that implements a core Access Policy granting permissions to users based on their external roles, resolved through a swappable repository (default source: settings.php).
project_description: External Roles is a developer-oriented framework module that extends Drupal's role-based access control through core's Access Policy API (Drupal 10.3+). It lets a site grant permissions to users based on "external" roles that originate outside Drupal's own role system — for example roles reported by an SSO/OpenID Connect identity provider or another external system. The module stores a user's external roles in an unlimited-cardinality string base field on the user entity (database table user__external_roles), added via hook_entity_base_field_info() and the external_roles_update_10000() install hook. Roles are read and manipulated through the plain ExternalRolesUser wrapper (hasExternalRole/getExternalRoles/addExternalRole/removeExternalRole/resetExternalRoles). At permission-calculation time the tagged access_policy service ExternalRolesAccessPolicy adds a CalculatedPermissionsItem built from the external_roles service, which loads a user's external roles from the base-field table and maps each role to a permission set via ExternalRolesRepositoryInterface. The default ExternalRolesRepository reads the role->permission definition from $settings['external_roles'] in settings.php, but consuming modules can override the external_roles.repository service to source definitions from anywhere (a YAML file, config, a remote system, etc.). Efficient calculation depends on the user.external_roles cache context (ExternalRolesCacheContext); a cache rebuild is required whenever the external-role definition changes. The module ships no routes, controllers, permissions of its own, forms, config objects or config schema; it is pure developer plumbing meant to be driven from other modules' business logic. Maintained by Simon Bäse, sponsored by Factorial GmbH.
